title: Teach git how to diff and merge your file formats
summary: A changelog that conflicts every release, a binary that shows as gibberish, a generated file nobody should merge. `.gitattributes` lets you attach a diff driver, a merge driver or a union strategy per path.
mental_model: Git's default merge is line-based and format-blind. `.gitattributes` maps a path pattern to a named driver, and config defines what that name does — so behaviour travels with the repository and the implementation stays local.

steps.title: The changelog that conflicts every single time
steps.why: Two branches each add a line at the top of the changelog. Line-based merging sees one contested region and stops — even though the correct answer is obviously 'keep both'.

write.content:
# Changelog

- add temperature alerts
- initial release

# Changelog

- add dosing calibration
- initial release

steps.expect: A conflict over two lines that do not actually disagree.

steps.title: Abort and tell git the file is a union
steps.why: The built-in `union` driver keeps both sides' lines instead of conflicting. It is exactly right for append-only files — changelogs, allow-lists, contributor lists — and exactly wrong for source code.

write.content:
# Append-only: keep both sides rather than conflicting.
CHANGELOG.md merge=union

actions.run: git commit -q -m "Merge changelogs as a union"

steps.expect: The merge succeeds and both entries are present.

verify.label: both changelog entries survived, with no conflict

steps.title: A binary that git should not try to merge
steps.why: Marking a path `binary` is shorthand for `-diff -merge -text`: no diffing, no line-ending conversion, and a conflict you must resolve by choosing a whole file. That is honest — a merged binary would be corrupt.

write.content:
# Append-only: keep both sides rather than conflicting.
CHANGELOG.md merge=union

# Never diff or merge binaries.
*.bin binary

commands: git check-attr diff merge text -- logo.bin
steps.expect: A conflict git refuses to guess at, and a diff that says 'binary files differ' rather than printing bytes.

verify.label: diffing is disabled for the binary

steps.title: Resolve a binary the only way you can
steps.why: `checkout --ours` or `--theirs` takes one whole file. There is no middle ground, which is why binary assets belong in a review process rather than a merge algorithm.

steps.title: A generated file that should never be merged at all
steps.why: A custom driver named in `.gitattributes` and defined in config. `merge.ours.driver true` means 'succeed, keeping our version' — the file is regenerated afterwards, so merging it is wasted effort.

write.content:
# Append-only: keep both sides rather than conflicting.
CHANGELOG.md merge=union

# Never diff or merge binaries.
*.bin binary

# Generated: keep ours and regenerate; never hand-merge.
*.lock merge=keep-ours

# Do not ship internal files in release archives.
/.gitattributes export-ignore
/docs export-ignore

actions.run: git config merge.keep-ours.name "keep our version; the file is regenerated"
git commit -q -m "Add a keep-ours driver for generated files"
git commit -q -a -m "Regenerate the lock on the branch"
git commit -q -a -m "Regenerate the lock on main"

steps.expect: The merge completes with no conflict, keeping main's version of the lock.

verify.label: the custom driver kept our version without conflicting
verify.hint: *.lock merge=keep-ours plus git config merge.keep-ours.driver true

steps.title: Teach git to read a format it does not understand
steps.why: A `textconv` diff driver converts a file to text before diffing. Here it renders the binary's header; in real projects it is `pdftotext`, `exiftool` or a JSON pretty-printer — turning an unreadable diff into a reviewable one.

write.content:
CHANGELOG.md merge=union

*.bin diff=binhead

*.lock merge=keep-ours

/.gitattributes export-ignore
/docs export-ignore

actions.run: git commit -q -m "Add a textconv driver for binaries"

steps.expect: A readable diff of the converted text, where before you saw 'binary files differ'.

verify.label: the textconv driver made the binary diffable

steps.title: Keep internal files out of release archives
steps.why: `export-ignore` excludes paths from `git archive`. The release tarball ends up without your CI config, docs source or attributes file — a one-line-per-path way to control what ships.

verify.cmd: sh -c 'git archive --format=tar HEAD | tar -t | grep -c gitattributes'
verify.label: internal files are excluded from the release archive
the union driver merged both changelog entries
the custom keep-ours driver handled the generated file
the driver named in .gitattributes is defined in config
the binary conflict was resolved by choosing one whole file
the rules are committed, so they apply to everyone

pitfalls: `.gitattributes` names a driver; config defines it. The file travels with the repository, the definition does not — document the `git config merge.<name>.driver` line, or the attribute silently falls back to the default merge.
`merge=union` on source code produces files containing both sides' lines and no conflict marker — code that compiles into nonsense. Use it only for genuinely append-only files.
A `textconv` driver makes diffs readable but does not make merges possible. Binary merges still require picking a whole side.
`export-ignore` affects `git archive` only. It does not affect clones, so it is a packaging tool, not a privacy one.
Attributes are matched like gitignore patterns, last match wins. `git check-attr` is the only reliable way to know which rule applied.
